title: Outdoor Lens Notifications Might Make me CANCEL my subscription!!!
content: I used to love this app - and I pay for premium.  And it still has a ton of great features to track trails, and notify you if you’re off the trail.  But the new Outdoor Lens feature is SO ANNOYING I might just find another option!!!  Now, when I’m trying to take photos during a hike, it assumes I want to identify the species of the tree I photographed and takes me thru a whole bunch of prompts.  I accidentally added a photo to the lens logbook (for species identification) and now, every time I open the app it asks me if I want to identify that species.  And I can’t find a way to delete that from the logbook!!  Internet said I’d have to delete the ENTIRE activity (record of my hike), which I don’t want to do.  The constant push notifications from the stupid lens/species ID are overriding every useful feature and taking me away from enjoying my hike.  Having to literally stop hiking to get out of the automatic identification mode is a SHOW STOPPER.  AND you can’t turn off the lens/species identification feature without turning off ALL notifications (like, you know, the important ones for staying on-trail).  I’m about done with this.  AllTrails needs to fix this ASAP or you’re losing my business.  I’ll change my review when you give me back my PEACEFUL hiking experience not cluttered with app notifications asking me to buy into this new lens feature.  I hike to get away from tech, not get marketing and distractions in the middle of my hike before I can unpause my tracker to resume my hike.  Total ZERO stars for that AllTrails!!  The app literally trapped me in the middle of a species identification line of questions when I didn’t even WANT to do that and I couldn’t resume my hike until we finished that.  AWFUL, just AWFUL.  And now I’m getting asked about that dumb picture on every screen.  Make it stop!!!

title: Outdoor Lens Notifications Might Make me CANCEL my subscription!!!
content: I used to love this app - and I pay for premium.  And it still has a ton of great features to track trails, and notify you if you’re off the trail.  But the new Outdoor Lens feature is SO ANNOYING I might just find another option!!!  Now, when I’m trying to take photos during a hike, it assumes I want to identify the species of the tree I photographed and takes me thru a whole bunch of prompts.  I accidentally added a photo to the lens logbook (for species identification) and now, every time I open the app it asks me if I want to identify that species.  And I can’t find a way to delete that from the logbook!!  Internet said I’d have to delete the ENTIRE activity (record of my hike), which I don’t want to do.  The constant push notifications from the stupid lens/species ID are overriding every useful feature and taking me away from enjoying my hike.  Having to literally stop hiking to get out of the automatic identification mode is a SHOW STOPPER.  AND you can’t turn off the lens/species identification feature without turning off ALL notifications (like, you know, the important ones for staying on-trail).  I’m about done with this.  AllTrails needs to fix this ASAP or you’re losing my business.  I’ll change my review when you give me back my PEACEFUL hiking experience not cluttered with app notifications asking me to buy into this new lens feature.  I hike to get away from tech, not get marketing and distractions in the middle of my hike before I can unpause my tracker to resume my hike.  Total ZERO stars for that AllTrails!!  The app literally trapped me in the middle of a species identification line of questions when I didn’t even WANT to do that and I couldn’t resume my hike until we finished that.  AWFUL, just AWFUL.  And now I’m getting asked about that dumb picture on every screen.  Make it stop!!!

title: Great App for Hiking, with Room for Improvement
content:
I’ve been using AllTrails for over a year now, and it’s become one of my go-to apps whenever I’m hiking or exploring new areas. The interface is clean, easy to navigate, and the premium version is well worth the price. I especially like being able to download maps for offline use and track my progress with distance completed and remaining.

My biggest issue is that some trail ratings don’t always match the actual difficulty. I’ve come across a few trails marked as easy or moderate that turned out to be much more challenging than expected. There are also times when the mapped trail doesn’t perfectly line up with the actual path. It’s usually only off by a little, but it can still be confusing.

One feature I’d love to see is more real-time trail information, such as trail closures, maintenance updates, seasonal hazards like ticks, or recent wildlife sightings. That kind of community-driven safety information would make an already great app even better.

Overall, AllTrails has been a reliable companion on my hikes, and despite a few inaccuracies, I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys spending time outdoors.
